money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: The local currency is the Libyan Dinar (LYD). Libya law prohibits importing or exporting the Libyan Dinar. Libya is a cash-based economy. Debit cards, credit cards and traveller’s cheques are not often accepted, and ATMs are rare. Official exchange offices will not accept Australian dollars. Withdrawing money from banks may be difficult due to severe shortages of cash. The security situation sometimes disrupts banking services.

laws.rule: Women can be subject to unwanted attention and harassment in Libya. Women may also face movement restrictions when travelling without a mahram (male guardian). While male guardianship is not mandatory under Libyan law, Libyan authorities frequently enforce it. Sexual assaults on women and gender-based violence are common in Libya. Survivors of sexual assault and domestic violence have little recourse in Libya, and women who report sexual crimes may be accused of adultery. Women and girls in Libya, both dual nationals and foreigners, are at increased risk of forced marriage, abduction, and kidnapping in Libya.
laws.heading: Women travellers

laws.rule: Libyan law prohibits same-sex relationships. Same-sex marriage is also illegal. Convicted offenders face prison sentences.
laws.heading: LGBTQIA+ travellers

laws.rule: Penalties for drug offences are severe. They include the death penalty or life in jail. - Carrying or using drugs
laws.heading: Drugs

laws.rule: If you're involved in a business dispute, officials may: confiscate your passport not let you leave Libya until the dispute is settled.
laws.heading: Business disputes

laws.rule: Libya is an Islamic country. It's illegal to attempt to convert Muslims to another religion. This includes: evangelism and preaching a non-Islamic religion possessing or distributing religious material other than Islam engaging in other activities that promote a religion other than Islam engaging in blasphemy against Islam. Penalties can be severe and may include the death penalty.
laws.heading: Religious conversion

laws.rule: Serious crimes may attract the death penalty. Other penalties may appear harsh by Australian standards. In Libya, it's illegal to: have sex outside of marriage drink alcohol import or export alcohol, antiquities, pork and pork products and pornographic content take photos of military installations, personnel, and government buildings.

steps.step: Contact the nearest Libyan embassy or consulate for the visa.
Enter only at an official border crossing; officials may detain anyone who can't prove they did.
Register the passport at the police station closest to where you stay, on arrival.
